com.vector.cfg.model.view.config

Interface IModelView

  • All Superinterfaces:
    java.lang.Comparable<IModelView>
    All Known Subinterfaces:
    IInvariantEcucDefView, IInvariantValuesView, IInvariantView, IPostBuildInvariantEcucDefView, IPostBuildInvariantValuesView, IPostBuildInvariantView, IPostBuildPredefinedVariantView, IPostBuildView, IPredefinedVariantView

    @PublishedApi(value=ADDITIONS_ALLOWED)
 @Immutable
public interface IModelView
extends java.lang.Comparable<IModelView>
    This is the base-API of all model views.

    All method parameters and return values must be non-null unless documented otherwise.

    Implementations of this interface are comparable. This guarantees deterministic order of the model views in access methods of the IModelViewManager and generator access services. In detail: The order is implemented as the alphabetical order of the model view names.

    The three interfaces IUnfilteredView, IPreBuildView and IPostBuildView define special meaning.

    • The IUnfilteredView disables all other currently active views and also change modes.
    • The IPostBuildView also enables the corresponding IPreBuildView when it is activated.
    • The IPreBuildView deactivates the currently active IPostBuildView and replaces it with the IPostBuildUnfilteredView.

    • Method Detail

      • compareTo

        @PublishedMethod
int compareTo(IModelView o)

        Caution: IModelViews of different projects are NOT equal. So Comparable.compareTo(Object) will not yield 0 for views of different projects! If you want to compare variance definition, please use method hasSameVarianceDefinitionAs(IModelView).

        compareTo(IModelView) has a deterministic order over project boundaries, but does not specify the internal ordering, so you can sort IModelView of different projects.

        Specified by:
        compareTo in interface java.lang.Comparable<IModelView>

      • equals

        boolean equals(java.lang.Object other)

        Caution: IModelViews of different projects are NOT equal. So equals(Object) will always yield false for views of different projects! If you want to compare variance definition, please use method hasSameVarianceDefinitionAs(IModelView).

        Note: Only identity based equal is supported, so equals() for IModelView means the same as ==!

        Overrides:
        equals in class java.lang.Object

      • executeWithThisView

        @PublishedMethod
IModelViewExecutionContext executeWithThisView()
        Executes the code under visibility of this model view.

        The returned IModelViewExecutionContext must be used within a Java "try-with-resources" feature. It makes sure, that the old view is restored when the try is completed.

        Example: 

         
 public void foo(IModelView modelView) {

     try (final IModelViewExecutionContext context = modelView.executeWithThisView()) {
         // do some operations
         ...
     }
 }

        Returns:
        the i model view execution context

      • hasSameVarianceDefinitionAs

        @KeepSecretFromPublishedApi
boolean hasSameVarianceDefinitionAs(IModelView other)
        Returns true, if this IModelView and the other IModelView have the same variance definition and are of the same IModelView subtype. The same variance definition means have the same PreBuild and PostBuild values for each SwSysconst value or PostBuild criterion value.

        This will also work over different projects. So you can compare IModelView A from project Pa with IModelView B of project Pb, and this will yield true, if A and B have the same variance definition.

        This can be used to find a corresponding IModelView in a different project.

        Parameters:
        other - the other
        Returns:
        true, if both have the same type and variance definition.
